title: Showcase: the scratch rover, proven
summary: Present the rover built from scratch this season: the bench numbers, the printed chassis, the proportional fix and the one-metre square, live for the family.
materials: the rover with chassis, motors, H-bridge, ESP32, battery and the fabricated sensor board
the taped one-metre square from week 11
tri-fold science fair board or a large sheet of card
the Maker's Log, open to weeks 1, 10 and 11

steps.title: Plan the presentation
steps.body:
Set up the same one-metre square from week 11 exactly as it was. Write the season's key numbers on the science fair board. Include the week 1 light-load current and predicted runtime, the week 10 drift before correction, and the week 11 average distance off target.

Plan the presentation in this order.

1. Show the bare motors, H-bridge and ESP32 on the bench, the way the season started in week 1.

2. Show the printed chassis from week 10 and the drift it had before any correction.

3. Run the one-metre square once, live, with the fabricated sensor board mounted and reporting.

4. Show the board's numbers. Say whether the correction really made the square closer to accurate, or whether the gap was smaller than the wobble between runs.

Be ready for one question about the design loop, from a bare motor on the bench to a rover that holds a shape.

figure.alt: Four showcase stations left to right, numbered 1 to 4: the bare bench parts from week 1, the chassis that drifted in week 10, a live run of the one-metre square with the week 11 correction, and the fair board with all the season's numbers. Captions remind the presenter to run on the same taped square used for the real numbers and to report honestly whether the fix beat the run-to-run wobble.

items.s: Showcase order: bench, chassis, live run, board
Live run on the same taped square used for the real numbers
Honestly report whether the fix beat the run-to-run wobble

steps.title: Rehearse the run and the answer
steps.body:
Run the one-metre square once at demo speed on the same taped square used for the real numbers. Nothing about the setup should have quietly changed since week 11.

Practise the sentence that states the result honestly. Say whether the correction really cut the drift by more than the wobble between runs, or whether the evidence was closer than that.
checklist: The taped square matches the one used for the week 11 numbers
The board shows the week 1, week 10 and week 11 numbers
The live run completes on the same setup as the recorded numbers
I can answer one question about the design loop, honestly

steps.title: Show the family
steps.body:
Gather the family and run the presentation in the order rehearsed: the bare bench parts, the drifting chassis, the live run, and the board's numbers. Invite one question and answer it as honestly as the data allows.

End by naming one thing that would make the test fairer next time.

steps.title: Show it
steps.prompt: A short recording of the live square run in front of the family, plus a photo of the board with all the season's numbers
